# grow.

> grow is a free, open source OBS overlay that shows a stream's to-do list. Viewers add tasks in Twitch chat with !task and finish them with !done, and the list updates live in OBS. It was built for study and cowork streams.

Hosted at https://grow.shiftbloom.studio. Source code: https://github.com/shiftbloom-studio/grow (AGPL-3.0-or-later). Made by shiftbloom studio, Hamburg.

## How it works

- A streamer makes an overlay at https://grow.shiftbloom.studio/app and gets two things: a dashboard key (their login, shown once) and an overlay link for an OBS Browser source.
- grow reads Twitch chat anonymously, without a bot account, and only while the overlay or dashboard is open.
- Every change reaches all open overlays and the dashboard over WebSockets within about a second.

## Chat commands

- `!task <text>` (also `!add`, `!todo`): add a task
- `!done [n]` (also `!check`, `!finish`): finish your first open task, or your n-th task
- `!undo [n]` (also `!uncheck`): reopen a task
- `!edit [n] <text>`: change a task
- `!remove [n]` (also `!delete`, `!rm`): delete a task
- `!mytasks` (also `!tasks`): highlight your tasks on the overlay
- `!cleardone`, `!clearall`, `!clearuser @name`: for the streamer and moderators

Full reference with examples: https://grow.shiftbloom.studio/commands

## Limits

- Twitch only for now. YouTube and Kick chat are not supported.
- Default limit of 3 open tasks per viewer and 150 tasks per list, both adjustable (1 to 20, 5 to 500).
- Tasks are capped at 140 characters.
- The overlay link is read-only. Anyone with the dashboard key can change the list and settings.
- There is no public API. The dashboard talks to the server over a WebSocket that needs a session cookie.

## Self-hosting

grow runs on Cloudflare Workers with one Durable Object per channel and a D1 database. The README explains how to deploy your own copy: https://github.com/shiftbloom-studio/grow#self-hosting
